content.title: About
content.content: Beef jerky is dried, seasoned strips of lean beef that are marinated in a blend of spices and then slowly dried at low temperature. The result is a dense, flavorful, long‑lasting snack with a characteristic salty‑spicy taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef jerky originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient way to preserve meat for travel and outdoor trips.
Traditionally, lean cuts of beef are used to keep fat content low and extend shelf life.
Protein content in jerky can reach up to 50 % of the product’s weight.
Different brands use unique spice blends, ranging from classic black pepper to smoked chipotle.
Jerky is often included in athletes’ diets as a quick source of amino acids.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Jerky provides a concentrated source of complete protein, essential for muscle repair and metabolic function.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, jerky contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is vital for normal blood formation and nervous system health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Jerky is often salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some varieties contain nitrites or artificial flavorings, which may be undesirable for sensitive individuals.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rarely, people can have an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Certain jerky products are made from fattier cuts, increasing calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beef jerky is convenient as a standalone snack, can be added to salads, soups, or used in dishes like fried rice. Break it into smaller pieces to top meals or simply enjoy straight from the pack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store jerky in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent mold growth. Shelf life is usually indicated on the packaging.
